name: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (V15)
note: CompTIA scores A+ Core 1 on a 100–900 scale with 675 to pass. This practice exam reports a straight percentage; treat 80% as your readiness bar. The real exam also includes performance-based questions (PBQs), which this practice exam doesn't include, so practice hands-on tasks separately. A+ certification requires passing both Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202). Questions follow the 220-1201 exam objectives (version 3.0).

questions.stem: A laptop runs only 40 minutes on a full charge, and its battery health shows 55%. What should the technician do?
options: Recalibrate the battery by draining it
questions.explanation: Battery capacity degrades over charge cycles. Low health means the battery should be replaced with a compatible part.

questions.stem: A user wants a laptop to boot and load apps faster. Which upgrade usually gives the biggest improvement?
options: Replace the webcam with a 4K model
Replace the HDD with an SSD
questions.explanation: SSDs have much faster access times than spinning hard drives, which speeds up boot and application loading.

questions.stem: Which memory form factor do most laptops use?
questions.explanation: Small outline DIMMs are compact modules for laptops and small form factor systems. Desktops typically use full-size DIMMs.

questions.stem: After a laptop's display was replaced, Wi-Fi signal is weak. What was likely disturbed during the repair?
options: The keyboard ribbon cable and connector
The Wi-Fi antenna leads in the display lid
questions.explanation: Laptop Wi-Fi antennas usually run through the display lid. They can be pinched, disconnected, or misrouted during screen replacement.

questions.stem: A company wants laptops that unlock with the user's fingerprint. Which component provides this?
questions.explanation: Biometric readers, such as fingerprint sensors, provide physical security and convenient authentication.

questions.stem: Employees tap their badges on a laptop's palm rest to sign in. Which feature supports this?
questions.explanation: Near-field (NFC) scanners read badges or cards at close range for authentication.

questions.stem: A user's laptop microphone records no sound in video calls, but the headset mic works. What should be checked first?
options: The battery's charge level and health
The SSD's firmware version and health
The mic's privacy switch and settings
questions.explanation: Many laptops have hardware or software privacy controls for mics and cameras. Checking these and app permissions comes before hardware replacement.

questions.stem: A laptop's webcam shows a black image, and the camera light doesn't turn on. The laptop has a physical slider above the lens. What should be checked first?
options: Whether the privacy shutter is closed
Whether the Wi-Fi card is enabled
Whether the RAM is seated correctly
questions.explanation: Physical privacy shutters block the camera. Checking simple causes first saves time.

questions.stem: A laptop user wants to connect to an external monitor, keyboard, mouse, and wired network through one cable at their desk. Which accessory fits?
questions.explanation: Docking stations, often over USB-C or Thunderbolt, provide display, peripheral, network, and power connections through one link.

questions.stem: A user's laptop has no internet, but their phone has 5G. How can the laptop get online through the phone?
options: Pair the phone as a Bluetooth keyboard
Use the phone as a hotspot or tethered connection
Use the phone as a port replicator
Connect the phone as an NFC reader for the laptop
questions.explanation: Tethering or a mobile hotspot shares the phone's cellular data connection over Wi-Fi, USB, or Bluetooth.

questions.stem: Which connector is reversible and used by most modern Android phones and laptops for charging and data?
questions.explanation: USB-C is reversible and supports data, power delivery, and video. MicroUSB and MiniUSB are older, non-reversible connectors.

questions.stem: Which wireless technology lets a phone make contactless payments by holding it near a terminal?
questions.explanation: Near-field communication works at a few centimeters and is used for contactless payments and badge readers.

questions.stem: What's the difference between a port replicator and a docking station?
options: There's no difference at all; the two terms always mean the same thing
A replicator mainly extends ports; a dock adds more features
A port replicator works only wirelessly; a dock needs cables
A port replicator charges devices; a dock can't provide power
questions.explanation: Port replicators simply extend the laptop's ports. Docking stations often add extra capabilities, such as additional displays, drive bays, or charging.

questions.stem: A designer wants to draw directly on a tablet screen with pressure sensitivity. Which accessory fits?
questions.explanation: Active styluses support pressure sensitivity and precise input on compatible touch screens.

questions.stem: A user can't pair Bluetooth earbuds with a phone. What's a correct first step?
options: Remove the SIM card and reinsert it
Disable Wi-Fi and restart the cellular modem
Reset all network settings on the phone
questions.explanation: Bluetooth pairing steps are: enable Bluetooth, enable pairing mode, find the device, enter a PIN if needed, and test connectivity.

questions.stem: A traveler wants to add a second phone number for a foreign carrier without inserting a physical card. Which technology supports this?
questions.explanation: An eSIM is an embedded SIM that can be provisioned digitally with a carrier profile.

questions.stem: A company wants to push Wi-Fi settings, require passcodes, and remotely wipe corporate data on employee phones. Which solution fits?
questions.explanation: MDM enforces configurations and policies, deploys corporate apps, and can wipe devices or corporate data.

questions.stem: On a BYOD phone enrolled in MDM, what can the company typically wipe if the employee leaves?
questions.explanation: BYOD management usually separates work and personal data, so only corporate data is removed with a selective wipe.

questions.stem: A user's phone shows the wrong location in maps, though GPS is enabled. Which other service helps determine location?
questions.explanation: Location services combine GPS with cellular and Wi-Fi data to estimate position, especially indoors.

questions.stem: A user's phone stopped syncing large files to cloud storage partway through the month. What should be checked?
options: Whether the screen brightness is low
Whether the stylus battery is low
Whether the data cap was reached
questions.explanation: Data caps can throttle or stop sync over cellular. Syncing over Wi-Fi or adjusting sync settings can help.

questions.stem: A new employee's phone isn't showing company calendar events. Which sync setting should be checked?
questions.explanation: Calendars, contacts, and mail sync through account settings, such as Exchange or Google accounts.

questions.stem: A phone needs to connect to a laptop over Bluetooth, and the laptop displays a six-digit code. What should the user do?
options: Type the code into the browser
Enter the code into the SIM settings
Confirm the matching code on the phone
questions.explanation: Pairing often requires confirming or entering a PIN on both devices to complete secure pairing.

questions.stem: A user disables cellular data while traveling abroad to avoid roaming charges but still needs email. What should they use?
questions.explanation: With cellular data disabled, Wi-Fi provides data connectivity for email and apps.

questions.stem: A company issues corporate-owned phones that employees can't use for personal apps. Which MDM configuration is this?
questions.explanation: Corporate configurations give the company full control. BYOD configurations protect corporate data while respecting personal use.

questions.stem: Which cellular generation offers the highest speeds and lowest latency?
questions.explanation: 5G provides higher throughput and lower latency than 4G LTE and older generations.

questions.stem: An employee's phone can't open a corporate app that MDM marks as required. What should the technician check?
options: Whether the phone uses a USB-C cable
Whether the screen protector is installed
Whether the phone's stylus is paired
questions.explanation: MDM distributes and manages corporate applications, so the device must be enrolled and assigned the app.

questions.stem: A laptop has a pointing stick in the middle of the keyboard. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Track points (pointing sticks) are small joysticks between keys that control the cursor.

questions.stem: A user wants wireless audio while video conferencing on a laptop. Which accessory and connection fit best?
questions.explanation: Bluetooth headsets pair with the laptop to provide wireless audio and a microphone for calls. A stylus, NFC tag, or port replicator doesn't carry audio.

questions.stem: An older iPhone uses which proprietary connector for charging and data?
questions.explanation: Older iPhones use Apple's Lightning connector. Newer iPhone models switched to USB-C.

questions.stem: Which port does an email client use to download mail with POP3?
questions.explanation: POP3 uses 110 to download mail, usually removing it from the server. IMAP uses 143, SMTP uses 25 to send mail, and HTTPS uses 443.

questions.stem: A user wants mail kept on the server and synced across a phone and laptop. Which protocol and port fit?
questions.explanation: IMAP keeps messages on the server and syncs folders across devices. POP3 typically downloads and removes mail from the server.

questions.stem: Which protocol sends outgoing email between mail servers?
questions.explanation: SMTP (port 25) transfers mail between servers and from clients to servers. POP3 and IMAP retrieve mail.

questions.stem: A technician needs to remotely control a Windows desktop graphically. Which port must be open?
questions.explanation: Remote Desktop Protocol uses 3389. SSH uses 22, Telnet uses 23, and 3306 is the default port for MySQL databases.

questions.stem: Which protocol sends commands to a remote device in plaintext and should be replaced with SSH?
questions.explanation: Telnet (port 23) sends everything, including passwords, unencrypted. SSH (port 22) encrypts the session.

questions.stem: Which ports are used by NetBIOS over TCP/IP for legacy Windows name and session services?
questions.explanation: NetBIOS/NetBT uses 137–139. FTP uses 20–21, DHCP uses 67–68, and SNMP uses 161–162.

questions.stem: Windows file sharing uses which port for SMB/CIFS?
questions.explanation: SMB/CIFS uses TCP 445 for file and printer sharing. LDAP uses 389, IMAP uses 143, and 5353 is multicast DNS (mDNS).

questions.stem: Which port does LDAP use to query a directory such as Active Directory?
questions.explanation: LDAP uses 389 to query directories such as Active Directory. Secure LDAP (LDAPS) uses 636, HTTPS uses 443, and RDP uses 3389.

questions.stem: What's the main difference between TCP and UDP?
options: TCP is used only for email; UDP is used only for web traffic
UDP is connection-oriented and reliable; TCP is connectionless
TCP is connection-oriented and reliable; UDP is connectionless
TCP works only on wireless networks; UDP works only on wired
questions.explanation: TCP uses a handshake, acknowledgments, and retransmission. UDP is faster with less overhead, which suits streaming, DNS queries, and VoIP.

questions.stem: Which protocol and port transfer files with separate control and data channels and no encryption?
questions.explanation: FTP uses 21 for control and 20 for data in active mode, and sends credentials in plaintext.

questions.stem: Which Wi-Fi band offers the longest range and best wall penetration but the fewest channels?
questions.explanation: 2.4 GHz travels farther and penetrates walls better, but it has only three non-overlapping channels and more interference.

questions.stem: A home user wants the fastest Wi-Fi on a new router and supported devices, using the 6 GHz band. Which standard is needed?
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi 6E extends 802.11ax into the 6 GHz band, and Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) also supports it. Wi-Fi 5 (802.11ac) and Wi-Fi 4 (802.11n) don't use 6 GHz.

questions.stem: A warehouse tracks pallets with tags that are read by scanners from a few meters away, without line of sight. Which technology is this?
questions.explanation: RFID tags are read by radio from short to moderate distances, which suits inventory tracking. NFC works only within a few centimeters.

questions.stem: Why might a Wi-Fi router's available channels differ between countries?
options: Channels depend on the router's color
Wi-Fi uses only one channel worldwide
Some countries don't allow encryption at all
questions.explanation: Regulatory bodies set allowed channels and power levels, so available channels vary by region.

questions.stem: A user wants maximum throughput in an apartment with few nearby networks. Which channel width setting helps on 5 GHz?
questions.explanation: Wider channels increase throughput when there's little interference. In crowded areas, narrower channels may perform better.

questions.stem: Which short-range wireless technology connects keyboards, mice, and headsets to a computer?
questions.explanation: Bluetooth creates personal area network connections for peripherals over short distances.

questions.stem: Which server automatically assigns IP addresses, subnet masks, and gateways to clients?
questions.explanation: DHCP servers lease IP configuration to clients. DNS resolves names, syslog collects logs, and NTP synchronizes time.

questions.stem: Which server keeps clocks synchronized across computers so logs and authentication work correctly?
questions.explanation: Network Time Protocol keeps clocks consistent. Time skew can break Kerberos authentication and confuse log timelines.

questions.stem: Which server role verifies users' identities and controls and records what they can access?
questions.explanation: AAA servers, such as RADIUS or TACACS+, handle authentication, authorization, and accounting.

questions.stem: Network devices send event messages to a central server for storage and review. What is this server?
questions.explanation: Syslog servers collect logs from many devices for troubleshooting and security monitoring.

questions.stem: A small business wants one appliance that combines firewall, antivirus, content filtering, and IDS/IPS. What should they buy?
options: A PoE injector with surge protection
questions.explanation: UTM appliances bundle multiple security functions into one device, which suits small organizations.

questions.stem: An appliance filters incoming email to block junk and phishing messages before they reach users. What is it?
questions.explanation: Spam gateways inspect inbound mail and block spam, phishing, and malware before messages reach users' mailboxes.

questions.stem: A factory's legacy system monitors and controls equipment across several remote sites. Which type of system is this?
questions.explanation: Supervisory control and data acquisition systems manage industrial processes. They're often legacy or embedded and need careful isolation.

questions.stem: Smart thermostats, cameras, and voice assistants that connect to a home network are examples of what?
questions.explanation: Internet of Things devices are network-connected embedded devices. They often need separate networks and firmware updates for security.

questions.stem: Which DNS record type holds SPF, DKIM, and DMARC policies for email authentication?
questions.explanation: TXT records store text data, including SPF, DKIM, and DMARC entries that help receiving servers detect spoofed mail.

questions.stem: Which email authentication method lets a domain owner tell receiving servers whether to reject or quarantine messages that fail SPF or DKIM?
questions.explanation: DMARC sets the policy for failed checks and requests reports. SPF lists allowed senders, and DKIM signs messages.

questions.stem: Which email authentication method adds a digital signature to outgoing messages so receivers can verify they weren't altered?
questions.explanation: DomainKeys Identified Mail signs messages with a private key, and receivers check the signature using a public key in DNS.

questions.stem: A DNS record maps mail.example.com to 203.0.113.10. Which record type is this?
questions.explanation: A records map a hostname to an IPv4 address. AAAA records map to IPv6 addresses.

questions.stem: A DHCP server should never hand out 192.168.1.1–192.168.1.20 because those are used by servers. What should be configured?
questions.explanation: Exclusions remove addresses from the DHCP pool. Reservations assign a specific address to a specific device.

questions.stem: What does a DHCP scope define?
options: The VLAN each switch port belongs to
The encryption method used for all Wi-Fi traffic
The list of websites users are allowed to visit
The address range and settings to hand out
questions.explanation: A scope is the pool of addresses for a subnet, along with options such as the gateway and DNS servers.

questions.stem: A DHCP lease time is set to eight days on a busy guest network, and addresses run out. What would help?
questions.explanation: Shorter leases return unused addresses to the pool faster, which suits networks with many transient devices.

questions.stem: A company separates its phones, guest devices, and staff PCs into different logical networks on the same switches. What is this?
questions.explanation: VLANs logically segment a switched network, improving security and reducing broadcast traffic.

questions.stem: A remote employee needs encrypted access to internal resources over the internet. What should they use?
questions.explanation: Virtual private networks create encrypted tunnels across untrusted networks such as the internet. VLANs segment local networks but don't encrypt remote traffic.

questions.stem: A small office needs a switch it can configure with VLANs and monitor remotely. Which type should they buy?
questions.explanation: Managed switches support configuration, such as VLANs, QoS, and monitoring. Unmanaged switches are plug-and-play with no settings.

questions.stem: An access point needs power, but the existing switch doesn't support PoE. What's the simplest fix?
questions.explanation: A PoE injector adds power to an Ethernet cable between a non-PoE switch and the powered device.

questions.stem: A home receives internet service over fiber, and a box on the wall converts the incoming light signal to Ethernet. What is this device?
options: A wireless access point with PoE
A DSL modem with a splitter
questions.explanation: The ONT terminates fiber service at the customer premises. Cable modems use coax, and DSL modems use telephone lines.

questions.stem: Which device forwards traffic between different networks, such as a home LAN and the internet?
questions.explanation: Routers connect networks and forward traffic by IP address. Switches connect devices within a network.

questions.stem: What uniquely identifies a network interface card at Layer 2?
questions.explanation: MAC addresses are 48-bit hardware addresses assigned to NICs and used for local delivery on Ethernet.

questions.stem: Which device filters traffic based on rules to protect a network from unauthorized access?
questions.explanation: Firewalls allow or block traffic based on rules about addresses, ports, protocols, and applications.

questions.stem: An internet connection uses existing telephone lines. Which device does the customer need?
questions.explanation: DSL delivers internet over telephone copper. Cable modems use coax, and ONTs terminate fiber.

questions.stem: A home router hands out addresses in 192.168.1.0/24. What type of addresses are these?
questions.explanation: 192.168.0.0/16 is a private range. The router uses NAT to share one public address for internet access.

questions.stem: A printer must keep the same IP address so users can always reach it. What's a common SOHO approach?
options: Assign a static IP or DHCP reservation
Let it pick a new address each day
questions.explanation: A static IP or a DHCP reservation keeps a printer's address consistent, so mapped printers and ports keep working.

questions.stem: A PC has the address 192.168.1.50 and mask 255.255.255.0. What is its gateway most likely to be?
questions.explanation: The default gateway must be on the same subnet. SOHO routers commonly use .1 or .254 on the local network.

questions.stem: Which addressing type uses 128-bit addresses written in hexadecimal?
questions.explanation: IPv6 addresses are 128 bits, written as eight groups of hexadecimal digits. IPv4 uses 32-bit dotted-decimal addresses.

questions.stem: A rural home has no cable or fiber, and a provider beams internet from a nearby tower to an antenna on the roof. Which connection type is this?
questions.explanation: WISPs deliver fixed wireless internet from towers to customer antennas, which is common in rural areas.

questions.stem: Which internet connection type usually has the highest latency because signals travel to orbit and back?
questions.explanation: Satellite connections, especially geostationary ones, have high latency. Low-earth orbit services reduce it but still vary.

questions.stem: A city connects its government buildings across town with a high-speed network. Which network type is this?
questions.explanation: A metropolitan area network spans a city or campus area, larger than a LAN but smaller than a WAN.

questions.stem: A user's smartwatch, phone, and earbuds connect to each other over Bluetooth. Which network type is this?
questions.explanation: Personal area networks connect devices around one person over short distances, usually with Bluetooth. MANs and WANs span much larger areas.

questions.stem: Which network type provides high-speed, block-level storage access to servers?
questions.explanation: Storage area networks connect servers to shared block storage, often over Fibre Channel or iSCSI.

questions.stem: A technician needs to attach an RJ45 connector to the end of a network cable. Which tool is used?
questions.explanation: Crimpers press RJ45 connectors onto cable ends. Punchdown tools seat wires into patch panels and keystone jacks.

questions.stem: A technician is terminating cable runs into a patch panel. Which tool seats the wires?
questions.explanation: Punchdown tools push wires into IDC terminals on patch panels and keystone jacks and trim the excess.

questions.stem: A technician wants to test whether a NIC port can send and receive without connecting to another device. Which tool fits?
questions.explanation: Loopback plugs route a port's transmit pins back to its receive pins so diagnostics can test the port.

questions.stem: A graphic designer needs an LCD monitor with the most accurate colors and widest viewing angles. Which panel type fits best?
questions.explanation: In-plane switching panels offer the best color accuracy and viewing angles. TN panels are fast but have weaker color and angles, and VA sits in between with strong contrast.

questions.stem: A competitive gamer wants a cheap LCD with the fastest response time and doesn't care about color accuracy. Which panel type fits?
questions.explanation: Twisted nematic panels are inexpensive with very fast response times but have poorer color and viewing angles.

questions.stem: Which display technology produces light per pixel, giving true blacks without a backlight?
questions.explanation: OLED pixels emit their own light and can turn off completely. LCDs need a backlight, such as LED or Mini-LED.

questions.stem: An older laptop's screen is very dim, but an image is faintly visible with a flashlight. Which component has likely failed?
questions.explanation: CCFL-backlit displays use an inverter to power the backlight. A failed inverter or backlight leaves a faint image.

questions.stem: A tablet displays images correctly but doesn't respond to touch. Which component has likely failed?
questions.explanation: The digitizer converts touch input into signals. It can fail while the display panel still shows images.

questions.stem: What does a monitor's refresh rate measure?
options: The range of colors the display can show
How often the image is redrawn per second
How many pixels fit in one inch of the screen
The maximum brightness of the backlight
questions.explanation: Refresh rate, in hertz, is how often the screen updates. Pixel density is pixels per inch, and color gamut is the range of colors.

questions.stem: A photo editor needs a monitor that can display a wide range of colors, such as most of DCI-P3. Which attribute matters most?
questions.explanation: Color gamut describes the range of colors a display can reproduce, often given as a percentage of sRGB or DCI-P3.

questions.stem: Which wiring standard is most commonly used for new Ethernet installations in the US?
questions.explanation: T568A and T568B define pin assignments. T568B is common in US commercial installs, and using the same standard on both ends makes a straight-through cable.

questions.stem: A cable must be buried underground between two buildings without a conduit. Which cable type fits?
questions.explanation: Direct-burial cable has a jacket rated for moisture and soil. Indoor cable isn't designed for underground use.

questions.stem: Which video connector carries both digital video and audio and is common on TVs and consoles?
questions.explanation: HDMI carries digital audio and video. VGA is analog video only, and DVI carries video without audio in most implementations.

questions.stem: Which video interface is analog and uses a 15-pin connector?
questions.explanation: VGA (DE-15) carries analog video only and is found on older monitors and projectors. HDMI, DisplayPort, and USB-C carry digital video.

questions.stem: A single port on a laptop supports 40 Gbps data, daisy-chained displays, and charging with a USB-C connector. Which technology is this?
questions.explanation: Thunderbolt 3 and later use the USB-C connector and support high-speed data, video, and power delivery.

questions.stem: An external hard drive enclosure connects with a dedicated external SATA port. Which connector is this?
questions.explanation: eSATA provides an external SATA connection. Molex is an older internal power connector, and DB9 is a serial connector.

questions.stem: An older lab instrument connects to a PC with a 9-pin serial cable. Which connector is this?
questions.explanation: DB9 is commonly used for RS-232 serial connections, such as console cables and legacy equipment.

questions.stem: Which connector is used for analog telephone lines and DSL?
questions.explanation: RJ11 is a smaller connector used for analog phone lines and DSL. RJ45 is the larger connector used for Ethernet.

questions.stem: Which connector supplies power to older IDE drives and some case fans from the power supply?
questions.explanation: 4-pin Molex connectors provide 5 V and 12 V power to legacy drives and accessories.

questions.stem: What is the maximum data rate of USB 3.0 (USB 3.2 Gen 1)?
questions.explanation: USB 3.0 (USB 3.2 Gen 1) supports 5 Gbps. USB 2.0 supports 480 Mbps, and 20 and 40 Gbps belong to newer USB and Thunderbolt versions.

questions.stem: A user needs to connect a laptop with only HDMI output to a projector with only VGA input. What do they need?
questions.explanation: HDMI is digital and VGA is analog, so an active adapter is needed to convert the signal. A passive cable can't convert digital to analog.

questions.stem: A server must detect and correct single-bit memory errors automatically. Which RAM type is needed?
questions.explanation: Error-correcting code memory detects and fixes single-bit errors. It needs motherboard and CPU support.

questions.stem: A user installed one 16 GB DIMM and wants better memory performance. What should they do?
options: Install the DIMM in a PCIe slot instead
Disable XMP memory profiles in the BIOS
Add a matching DIMM for dual-channel
Replace it with a SODIMM laptop module
questions.explanation: Matched modules in the proper slots enable dual-channel mode, increasing memory bandwidth.

questions.stem: Can a DDR4 module be installed in a DDR5 motherboard slot?
options: Only if the BIOS is updated
No, the notches and voltages differ
Yes, DDR versions are fully interchangeable
questions.explanation: Each DDR generation has a different key notch and electrical requirements, so they aren't interchangeable.

questions.stem: Which SSD interface connects directly to PCIe lanes for the highest performance?
questions.explanation: NVMe is designed for flash storage over PCIe and is much faster than SATA-based SSDs.

questions.stem: A technician installs an M.2 drive, but the system only runs it at SATA speeds. What's the likely reason?
options: The RAM isn't in dual-channel mode
The drive needs a separate Molex power cable
M.2 drives always run at SATA speeds
It's an M.2 SATA drive or slot
questions.explanation: M.2 is a form factor that can carry SATA or PCIe/NVMe. The drive and slot must both support NVMe for full speed.

questions.stem: Which RAID level stripes data across disks with no redundancy?
questions.explanation: RAID 0 stripes data for performance but has no redundancy, so the whole array is lost if any one disk fails.

questions.stem: Which RAID level mirrors data across two disks?
questions.explanation: RAID 1 duplicates data on two drives, so either drive can fail without data loss.

questions.stem: Which RAID level uses striping with distributed parity and survives one disk failure with at least three disks?
questions.explanation: RAID 5 needs at least three disks and tolerates one failure. RAID 6 uses double parity and tolerates two.

questions.stem: An array must survive two simultaneous disk failures. Which RAID level fits?
questions.explanation: RAID 6 uses two parity blocks, so it tolerates two disk failures and needs at least four disks.

questions.stem: Which RAID level combines mirroring and striping and needs at least four disks?
questions.explanation: RAID 10 stripes across mirrored pairs, giving high performance and redundancy. It needs at least four disks and uses half the raw capacity.

questions.stem: Which drive interface is common in enterprise servers and supports dual-port connections for redundancy?
questions.explanation: Serial Attached SCSI is designed for enterprise reliability and performance, with features such as dual-porting.

questions.stem: A user wants the smallest motherboard form factor for a compact home theater PC. Which fits?
questions.explanation: Mini-ITX boards are 170 × 170 mm, smaller than microATX and ATX, which suits small form factor builds.

questions.stem: Which firmware setting prevents unsigned bootloaders and boot-level malware from loading?
questions.explanation: Secure Boot, a UEFI feature, verifies that bootloaders are signed by trusted keys.

questions.stem: BitLocker needs a hardware chip that stores encryption keys and measures boot integrity. Which component is this?
questions.explanation: The Trusted Platform Module stores keys and supports measured boot. HSMs are dedicated, often external, key management devices.

questions.stem: A bank needs a dedicated, tamper-resistant device to generate and protect large numbers of cryptographic keys for servers. What should it use?
options: A Trusted Platform Module in each PC
questions.explanation: HSMs are specialized devices for secure key generation, storage, and cryptographic operations at scale.

questions.stem: A user can't run virtual machines in a hypervisor, and it reports that hardware virtualization is unavailable. What should be checked?
options: Whether the boot password is set
Whether virtualization is enabled in firmware
Whether the case fans are running at full speed
questions.explanation: Hardware virtualization, Intel VT-x or AMD-V, must be enabled in BIOS/UEFI for most hypervisors to run virtual machines.

questions.stem: A company wants to prevent users from booting computers from USB drives. Where should this be configured?
options: In BIOS/UEFI boot and USB settings
In the router's DHCP scope options page
questions.explanation: Firmware settings control boot order and can disable USB booting. A BIOS password stops users from changing them.

questions.stem: Which processor architecture is common in smartphones and many power-efficient laptops?
questions.explanation: ARM uses a reduced instruction set focused on power efficiency. x86/x64 dominates traditional desktops and servers.

questions.stem: When installing a CPU and cooler, what should be applied between the CPU and heat sink?
options: Thermal paste or a thermal pad
questions.explanation: Thermal compound fills microscopic gaps so heat transfers efficiently from the CPU to the heat sink.

questions.stem: A streamer wants to record gameplay from a console on a PC. Which expansion card fits?
questions.explanation: Capture cards ingest video from external sources, such as consoles or cameras, for recording or streaming.

questions.stem: Which motherboard connector does a modern GPU typically use?
questions.explanation: Graphics cards use PCIe x16 slots for maximum bandwidth. PCI is an older, slower standard.

questions.stem: Front-panel USB ports and the power button connect to which part of the motherboard?
questions.explanation: Motherboard headers provide connections for front-panel controls, USB, audio, and fans.

questions.stem: A workstation board has two CPU sockets. What must be true of the processors installed?
options: They must be supported matching models
They can be any mix of AMD and Intel
They must use different socket types
Only one socket can ever be used
questions.explanation: Multisocket boards require compatible, usually identical, CPUs that match the socket and chipset.

questions.stem: A user is moving a PC to a country that uses 230 V power. What should be checked on the power supply?
options: Whether it has an 80 Plus rating
Whether it has a modular cable
questions.explanation: Power supplies must support the local input voltage, either auto-switching or through a selector switch.

questions.stem: Which power supply output voltage powers CPUs and GPUs?
questions.explanation: The 12 V rail supplies high-power components such as CPUs, GPUs, and drive motors. 3.3 V and 5 V power logic circuits.

questions.stem: A builder wants to reduce cable clutter by attaching only the power cables a system needs. Which PSU type fits?
questions.explanation: Modular PSUs have detachable cables, so builders attach only what they need, improving airflow and cable management.

questions.stem: A critical server must keep running if one power supply fails. What should it have?
questions.explanation: Redundant, hot-swappable power supplies let a server keep running when one unit fails.

questions.stem: What does an 80 Plus Gold rating on a power supply indicate?
options: High energy efficiency at typical loads
A higher maximum wattage than other PSUs
questions.explanation: 80 Plus ratings measure power supply efficiency at set loads. Higher tiers, such as Gold or Platinum, waste less power as heat. They don't indicate wattage.

questions.stem: Which connector supplies main power to a modern ATX motherboard?
questions.explanation: ATX boards use a 24-pin main connector, often supplied as 20+4 pins for compatibility with older boards.

questions.stem: A Mac user needs a printer driver that handles complex graphics consistently across platforms. Which page description language fits best?
questions.explanation: PostScript is device-independent and handles complex graphics well. PCL is common and efficient, especially on Windows.

questions.stem: Employees must tap their badges at a shared printer before their documents print. Which security feature is this?
questions.explanation: Secured print holds jobs until the user authenticates at the device, preventing others from picking up sensitive pages.

questions.stem: A company wants a record of who printed and scanned what on its multifunction devices. Which feature provides this?
questions.explanation: Audit logs record who printed, scanned, or copied what and when, supporting accountability and compliance.

questions.stem: Users want to scan documents directly to a shared network folder. Which scan service fits?
questions.explanation: Scan-to-SMB saves files to a network share. MFDs may also scan to email or cloud services.

questions.stem: A user needs to scan a 40-page stack of documents quickly. Which MFD feature helps?
options: The duplex print setting in the driver
questions.explanation: ADFs feed multiple pages automatically. Flatbeds suit single pages, books, and fragile items.

questions.stem: A laser printer has reached its page count for scheduled service. What should be installed?
questions.explanation: Laser maintenance kits typically include a fuser, rollers, and pads, replaced at recommended page counts.

questions.stem: Thermal receipt printer output is faint and streaked. What maintenance should be done?
options: Calibrate and align the printhead nozzles
Replace the toner cartridge and drum
Clean the heating element and remove debris
questions.explanation: Thermal printers need clean heating elements and the correct thermal paper. They don't use toner or ink.

questions.stem: An auto shop needs to print multipart carbon forms. Which printer type fits?
questions.explanation: Impact printers strike the paper through a ribbon, which transfers to multipart forms.

questions.stem: An inkjet printer's output has missing lines in some colors. What should be done first?
questions.explanation: Clogged nozzles cause missing lines. Cleaning printheads, then aligning or calibrating, usually fixes it.

questions.stem: A security team wants to open a suspicious file in an isolated environment that can be discarded afterward. What should they use?
options: A virtual machine as a sandbox
questions.explanation: VMs used as sandboxes isolate untrusted code from the host, and they can be reverted or deleted afterward.

questions.stem: Which hypervisor type runs directly on the hardware with no host operating system?
questions.explanation: Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisors, such as ESXi or Hyper-V Server, run directly on hardware. Type 2 runs as an application on a host OS.

questions.stem: A developer runs VirtualBox on a Windows laptop to test Linux. Which hypervisor type is this?
questions.explanation: Type 2 hypervisors run on top of a host operating system, which suits desktops and testing.

questions.stem: How do containers differ from virtual machines?
options: Containers can only run on physical servers
Containers need a Type 1 hypervisor to run at all
Containers each run a full OS; VMs share the host kernel
Containers share the host kernel; VMs run full OSs
questions.explanation: Containers package apps with dependencies and share the host kernel, so they're lightweight. VMs virtualize hardware and run separate operating systems.

questions.stem: A company delivers full desktops to employees from central servers so users can work from any device. What is this?
questions.explanation: VDI hosts desktop operating systems on servers and streams them to client devices.

questions.stem: A business still needs an application that only runs on Windows XP. How can it keep using it more safely?
options: Install Windows XP on every new PC
Run it as a cloud SaaS app
Run it in an isolated virtual machine
Connect XP directly to the internet
questions.explanation: Virtualization can run legacy software and operating systems in isolated VMs, limiting exposure.

questions.stem: A user wants to run a Linux-only application on a macOS laptop. Which approach fits?
options: A Type 1 hypervisor on a phone
questions.explanation: Cross-platform virtualization runs software built for one OS on a different host OS.

questions.stem: Which resource requirement is most important when planning to run several VMs on one host?
options: A monitor for each virtual machine
A dedicated printer for each virtual machine
A separate keyboard for each guest
questions.explanation: Each VM consumes host CPU, memory, storage, and network resources, so the host must be sized for the combined load.

questions.stem: Why should a VM's network settings be planned carefully?
options: Bridged, NAT, or isolated modes change exposure
VMs always share the host's IP address
VMs can't connect to any network at all
VM network settings can't be changed after creation
questions.explanation: Virtual network options determine whether a VM is reachable from the LAN, shares the host's address through NAT, or is isolated.

questions.stem: A VM running outdated software is compromised. Why is VM security still important?
options: VMs are automatically immune to malware
VMs need patching like physical systems
VMs delete themselves automatically after an infection
VMs can never reach the host network
questions.explanation: Guest OSs need updates, antivirus, and access controls. Hypervisors must also be patched to prevent VM escape attacks.

questions.stem: A developer needs a temporary environment to test a software update before deploying it to production. Which purpose of VMs is this?
questions.explanation: VMs make it easy to create, snapshot, and discard test environments without affecting production.

questions.stem: Which concept lets users run a single program in an isolated package without installing it locally?
questions.explanation: Application virtualization delivers apps that run isolated from the local OS, which helps with compatibility and management.

questions.stem: A company uses a hosted email and office suite that the provider fully manages. Which cloud model is this?
questions.explanation: Software as a service delivers complete applications. The customer manages only users, data, and settings.

questions.stem: Several hospitals share cloud infrastructure built for their common regulatory needs. Which deployment model is this?
questions.explanation: Community clouds are shared by organizations with common requirements, such as compliance.

questions.stem: A company keeps sensitive systems in its own datacenter and bursts extra workloads to a public cloud. Which model is this?
questions.explanation: Hybrid cloud combines private or on-premises infrastructure with public cloud services.

questions.stem: A company runs a cloud environment used only by itself, on dedicated infrastructure. Which deployment model is this?
questions.explanation: Private clouds serve one organization, either on-premises or hosted by a provider on dedicated resources.

questions.stem: A cloud bill includes charges for data transferred out of the provider's network. What is this charge for?
questions.explanation: Metered utilization often charges for egress (data leaving the cloud). Ingress is data coming in and is often free.

questions.stem: Cloud resources are billed only for the compute hours and storage actually used. Which characteristic is this?
questions.explanation: Metered (pay-as-you-go) billing charges based on actual consumption of compute, storage, and data transfer, such as egress.

questions.stem: An online store automatically adds servers for a holiday sale and removes them afterward. Which cloud characteristic is this?
questions.explanation: Elasticity scales resources up and down automatically to match demand, so the store pays only for the extra capacity while it's needed.

questions.stem: A user saves a document on a laptop, and it appears on their phone a moment later through the cloud. Which feature is this?
questions.explanation: Cloud file synchronization keeps copies of files consistent across a user's devices.

questions.stem: A provider runs many customers' virtual machines on the same physical hosts, with logical isolation between them. What is this?
questions.explanation: Multitenancy shares infrastructure among customers. Dedicated resources give one customer exclusive hardware.

questions.stem: A regulated company requires that its cloud VMs never share physical hardware with other customers. What should it choose?
questions.explanation: Dedicated hosts or instances provide physical isolation, usually at higher cost than shared resources.

questions.stem: A provider guarantees services stay reachable during a datacenter failure by running across multiple zones. Which characteristic is this?
questions.explanation: Availability is improved through redundancy across zones and regions, with failover.

questions.stem: A developer deploys a web app to a managed platform and doesn't manage the OS or runtime. Which model is this?
questions.explanation: Platform as a service provides managed runtimes and tools, so developers focus on code and data.

questions.stem: A company rents virtual servers and installs and patches the operating systems itself. Which model is this?
questions.explanation: Infrastructure as a service provides virtual hardware. The customer manages the OS, middleware, and apps.

questions.stem: A PC powers on but beeps in a repeating pattern and shows nothing on screen. What should the technician do?
options: Reset the CMOS and reboot repeatedly
Look up the POST beep code
questions.explanation: POST beep codes identify hardware failures, such as RAM or video, before the display initializes. Codes vary by firmware vendor.

questions.stem: A PC shows a blue stop error screen during heavy use and restarts. Which hardware should be tested first?
options: The RAM, with a memory diagnostic
questions.explanation: Faulty RAM commonly causes stop errors and crashes. Memory diagnostics can confirm it. Overheating and drivers are other common causes.

questions.stem: A PC shuts down randomly during games, and the CPU fan is caked with dust. What's the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Dust buildup reduces cooling, so the CPU overheats and the system shuts down to protect itself.

questions.stem: A technician notices bulging, leaking capacitors on a motherboard. What should be done?
questions.explanation: Swollen capacitors indicate failure and cause instability. The motherboard should be replaced.

questions.stem: A PC's clock resets to a date years ago every time it's unplugged. What should be replaced?
questions.explanation: The CMOS battery keeps firmware settings and the real-time clock when the PC has no power.

questions.stem: A user reports a burning smell from a desktop. What should the technician do first?
options: Power it off and unplug it
Run a disk check on the drive
questions.explanation: A burning smell can indicate a failing power supply or component. Remove power immediately for safety, then inspect.

questions.stem: A desktop is completely dead: no fans, no lights. The outlet works. What should be checked next?
options: The PSU's switch, cable, and output
questions.explanation: No power at all points to the power supply, its switch, or cabling. A PSU tester can confirm whether it outputs power.

questions.stem: A PC is sluggish, and Task Manager shows the CPU at 100% with temperatures near its limit. What's a likely cause?
options: A failing CMOS battery on the board
Too little free space on the system drive
questions.explanation: CPUs slow themselves when hot. Cleaning, reapplying thermal paste, or improving airflow restores performance.

questions.stem: A PC makes a loud grinding noise from inside the case near the CPU cooler. What's the likely cause?
questions.explanation: Unusual noise often comes from failing fan bearings. Replacing the fan prevents overheating.

questions.stem: A Mac displays a proprietary crash screen asking the user to restart. Which component is a common hardware cause?
questions.explanation: Proprietary crash screens, such as a macOS kernel panic, are often caused by faulty RAM, drivers, or other hardware.

questions.stem: After a RAM upgrade, a PC powers on but shows a blank screen and no POST. What should be checked first?
options: Whether the monitor needs a firmware update
Whether the keyboard layout is correct
Whether the RAM is compatible and seated
questions.explanation: Incompatible or poorly seated memory often prevents POST. Reseating or testing modules one at a time isolates the problem.

questions.stem: Several applications crash on a PC, and Event Viewer shows memory errors. What should the technician run?
options: A disk cleanup of temp files
questions.explanation: Repeated app crashes with memory errors suggest failing RAM. Windows Memory Diagnostic or MemTest86 can confirm it.

questions.stem: A hard drive makes a repeated clicking sound and files are becoming corrupted. What should the technician do?
options: Increase the virtual memory page file size
Back up the data and replace the drive
Defragment the drive to fix it
questions.explanation: Clicking often means mechanical failure. Back up what you can right away, then replace the drive.

questions.stem: Monitoring software reports a S.M.A.R.T. failure warning on a drive. What does this mean?
options: The drive is nearly out of free space
The drive predicts it may fail soon
The drive needs a driver update
questions.explanation: S.M.A.R.T. tracks drive health. Warnings indicate likely failure, so data should be backed up and the drive replaced.

questions.stem: A PC shows "bootable device not found" after a power outage. What should be checked first?
options: The boot order and drive detection
questions.explanation: Confirm that firmware detects the drive and that boot order is correct before assuming the drive has failed.

questions.stem: A RAID 5 array shows "degraded" after one disk failed. What should be done?
options: Replace the failed disk and rebuild the array
Delete the array and recreate it
Add the failed disk back without testing
questions.explanation: A degraded RAID 5 has lost redundancy. Replacing the failed disk and rebuilding restores protection, ideally after confirming backups.

questions.stem: A server's RAID controller sounds an audible alarm and a drive's LED is amber. What does this indicate?
options: The server's fans are running at full speed
A drive or array problem needing attention
questions.explanation: Audible alarms and amber or red LED indicators usually signal a failed or failing drive in an array.

questions.stem: A database server's disk response times are high, and monitoring shows low IOPS. What would most improve performance?
options: Adding more CPU cores to the server
Moving to SSDs or a faster RAID level
questions.explanation: Low IOPS limits disk-heavy workloads. SSDs or RAID 10 typically increase performance.

questions.stem: A newly installed second drive doesn't appear in File Explorer, but BIOS detects it. What should the technician do?
options: Initialize and format it in Disk Management
Change the SATA mode from AHCI to IDE
Replace the drive immediately under warranty
questions.explanation: New drives must be initialized, partitioned, and formatted in Disk Management before they appear as volumes in File Explorer.

questions.stem: After a motherboard replacement, a RAID array is reported as missing. What's a likely cause?
options: The new board needs more RAM installed
The drives need new SATA power cables
The RAID settings aren't on the new board
The drives were wiped by the new board
questions.explanation: Arrays depend on controller settings. A new board or controller may need RAID mode enabled or the array imported.

questions.stem: A drive takes much longer than usual to read and write files, and S.M.A.R.T. shows reallocated sectors increasing. What should be done?
options: Back up data and plan a replacement
questions.explanation: Extended read/write times and growing reallocated sectors suggest a failing drive.

questions.stem: A monitor shows "No signal," but the PC is running. What should be checked first?
options: The monitor's input source and cable
questions.explanation: An incorrect input source or loose cable is the most common cause of "No signal."

questions.stem: A projector shuts off by itself after 20 minutes, and its vents are clogged with dust. What's the likely cause?
options: A wrong color profile in Windows
A dead pixel in the DLP chip
questions.explanation: Projectors shut down to protect themselves from heat. Cleaning filters and vents fixes intermittent shutdowns.

questions.stem: A projector shows no image, its lamp indicator is lit, and it's past its rated lamp hours. What should be replaced?
questions.explanation: Projector lamps have limited lifespans. A burnt-out bulb causes no image or a very dim image.

questions.stem: A static taskbar remains faintly visible on an OLED screen even when other content is shown. What is this?
questions.explanation: Burn-in is permanent image retention from static content, especially on OLED displays.

questions.stem: Text on an LCD monitor looks blurry, even though the cable is fine. What should be checked?
options: That it's set to the native resolution
That the brightness is at 100 percent
That the refresh rate is set to the maximum
That the GPU driver supports HDR output
questions.explanation: LCDs have a fixed native resolution. Running them at a lower resolution forces scaling, which makes text look fuzzy.

questions.stem: A monitor shows one tiny spot that always stays black. What is this?
questions.explanation: Dead pixels stay dark, while stuck pixels stay one color. Both are panel defects, unlike burn-in, which is faint retained imagery.

questions.stem: Colors on a monitor look tinted purple after a cable was replaced. What's a likely cause?
options: A damaged cable or loose pin
questions.explanation: Incorrect colors often come from loose or damaged video cables, especially analog VGA with bent pins.

questions.stem: A user connects a laptop to a TV over HDMI, and video works but sound still comes from the laptop speakers. What should be changed?
questions.explanation: HDMI carries audio, but the OS must use the HDMI or TV device as its default audio output in sound settings.

questions.stem: A laptop screen flickers when the lid is moved. What's the likely cause?
options: A damaged display cable in the hinge
A failing laptop battery cell in the base
questions.explanation: Flicker that changes with lid movement points to the display cable running through the hinge.

questions.stem: The desktop doesn't fit the screen, with edges cut off on a TV. Which setting should be adjusted?
options: The TV's refresh rate and motion setting
The HDMI cable's version and length
The GPU driver's color depth setting
questions.explanation: TVs often overscan, cutting off the edges. Adjusting display scaling, overscan, or resolution settings fixes the fit.

questions.stem: A projected image is stretched into a trapezoid shape. What should be adjusted?
questions.explanation: Keystone correction fixes distortion caused when the projector isn't perpendicular to the screen.

questions.stem: A phone's case is bulging and the screen is lifting. What should the technician do?
options: Recalibrate the battery by fully draining it
Stop using it and replace the battery
questions.explanation: A swollen lithium-ion battery is a fire hazard. Power down, avoid puncturing it, and replace and recycle it properly.

questions.stem: A phone charges only when the cable is held at an angle. What's the likely cause?
options: A damaged or dirty charging port
questions.explanation: Physically damaged or lint-filled ports cause improper charging. Cleaning or replacing the port fixes it.

questions.stem: A phone was dropped in water and now behaves erratically. What should be done first?
options: Charge it immediately to test it
Use a hair dryer on high heat
Power it off and don't charge it
Install a new app to check sensors
questions.explanation: Liquid damage can short circuits. Powering off and keeping it unplugged reduces damage before inspection or repair.

questions.stem: A tablet's cursor moves on its own, and taps register in the wrong place. What should be checked?
options: Outdated apps from the app store
A weak Wi-Fi signal in the room
questions.explanation: Cursor drift and misplaced touches indicate digitizer or calibration problems. Recalibrating may help, but a damaged digitizer needs replacing.

questions.stem: A user can't install new apps on a phone, which shows a storage warning. What should be done?
questions.explanation: Insufficient storage prevents app installation. Removing unused apps and media or moving data to the cloud helps.

questions.stem: A phone runs hot, its battery drains fast, and it shows pop-up ads, even on the home screen. What's a likely cause?
questions.explanation: Malware can cause overheating, battery drain, unexpected ads, and degraded performance. Removing suspicious apps and scanning help.

questions.stem: A phone has no cellular signal in a location where other phones on the same carrier work. What should be checked first?
options: Airplane mode and the SIM/eSIM status
The phone's screen brightness and timeout
questions.explanation: Airplane mode, a disabled line, or a faulty SIM often cause no connectivity on one device.

questions.stem: A tablet's stylus doesn't work, but finger touch does. What should be checked?
options: The tablet's Wi-Fi channel and band
The stylus's charge and Bluetooth pairing
questions.explanation: Active styluses often need charging and pairing. Compatibility with the specific tablet also matters.

questions.stem: A phone has become slow after years of use, and its battery health is poor. What may be happening?
options: The screen protector is slowing the touch input
The OS is throttling to protect the battery
The SIM card is overloaded with contacts
The cellular carrier is limiting the CPU
questions.explanation: Some phones reduce performance when battery health is poor to prevent unexpected shutdowns. Replacing the battery can restore speed.

questions.stem: Users near a microwave lose Wi-Fi every time it runs. What's the likely cause?
options: An incorrect subnet mask on laptops
A weak WPA2 passphrase on the AP
A DHCP lease conflict on the router
questions.explanation: Microwave ovens operate near 2.4 GHz and can interfere with Wi-Fi. Using 5 GHz or moving devices helps.

questions.stem: A PC shows "No internet access" and has the address 169.254.10.5. What's the problem?
options: The DNS server is returning wrong records
It couldn't get an address from DHCP
questions.explanation: A 169.254.x.x APIPA address means the PC couldn't reach a DHCP server, so it can talk only to the local segment.

questions.stem: VoIP calls are choppy and robotic during busy hours. Which issue is the most likely cause?
options: An expired DHCP lease on the phones
An incorrect DNS server on phones
A duplicate IP address on one phone
questions.explanation: Real-time voice is sensitive to jitter, latency, and packet loss. QoS and more bandwidth improve call quality.

questions.stem: A switch log shows a port going up and down repeatedly. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Port flapping is a link repeatedly going up and down, often from a bad cable, faulty NIC, or duplex issues.

questions.stem: Users can't join the corporate Wi-Fi after their passwords changed, but other users connect fine. What's the likely issue?
options: A failed DHCP server for the whole site
A broken patch panel port in the closet
Channel overlap on the access points
questions.explanation: Outdated saved credentials cause authentication failures. Forgetting the network and reconnecting usually fixes it.

questions.stem: File transfers on the office network are much slower than usual. A technician finds a switch port negotiated 100 Mbps instead of 1 Gbps. What's a likely cause?
options: An incorrect DNS server setting on the PCs
A full DHCP scope on the office router
A misconfigured VLAN on the switch port
A damaged cable or wrong cable category
questions.explanation: Bad or low-category cabling can force lower link speeds, causing slow network performance.

questions.stem: A user's internet works for a few minutes, drops, and returns throughout the day. The modem's lights flicker during drops. What should be checked?
options: The ISP line and modem signal
questions.explanation: Intermittent internet often stems from ISP signal problems, modem issues, or line noise.

questions.stem: Ping times to a cloud application are 400 ms over a fiber connection. What does this indicate?
options: A duplex mismatch on the PC
High latency somewhere on the path
An APIPA address on the client
questions.explanation: High latency slows interactive apps. traceroute can help find where delay is introduced.

questions.stem: A laser printer prints a faint duplicate of the image lower on the page. What's the likely cause?
options: An incorrect print driver on the PC
A worn pickup roller in the main tray
Low toner in the cartridge for the job
A worn drum or fuser causing ghosting
questions.explanation: Double or echo images on laser prints usually point to the drum, cleaning blade, or fuser.

questions.stem: Laser printouts smear when touched right after printing. Which component is the likely cause?
questions.explanation: The fuser uses heat and pressure to bond toner to paper. If it fails, toner isn't fused and smears when touched.

questions.stem: A laser printer produces a vertical line down every page. What's a common cause?
options: A scratch or debris on the drum
questions.explanation: Lines down the page often come from a damaged drum, dirty corona wire, or debris in the paper path.

questions.stem: A printer outputs pages of random symbols and characters. What's the most likely cause?
options: Low toner in the main cartridge
A worn pickup roller in the tray
questions.explanation: Garbled print usually results from the wrong driver or a mismatched page description language.

questions.stem: A printer feeds several sheets at once. Which component should be checked?
questions.explanation: Worn separation pads and rollers cause multipage misfeeds. Humid or stuck-together paper can also contribute.

questions.stem: A printer doesn't pick up paper from the tray at all. What should be checked?
options: The toner cartridge and imaging drum
The fuser assembly and its heater
The transfer roller and its alignment
The pickup roller and the paper loading
questions.explanation: Paper not feeding is often caused by worn pickup rollers, incorrect paper loading, or tray settings.

questions.stem: Print jobs pile up in the queue and nothing prints, even after restarting the printer. What should be done on the print server?
options: Reinstall the print driver on clients
questions.explanation: A frozen queue is often fixed by clearing the queue and restarting the Print Spooler service.

questions.stem: Laser prints are faded across the whole page. What should be checked first?
options: The pickup roller in the main tray
The separation pad in the tray
The toner level and density setting
The paper tray guides and size
questions.explanation: Faded prints usually mean low toner or a low density setting. Economy modes also reduce darkness.

questions.stem: Pages print in portrait even though the user selected landscape in the app. What should be checked?
options: The orientation setting in the printer driver
The fuser temperature setting on the panel
questions.explanation: Incorrect page orientation is a software setting issue between the app and driver defaults.

questions.stem: A multifunction printer reports "tray 2 not installed" though the tray is attached. What should be checked?
questions.explanation: Drivers must have installable options configured so the system recognizes added trays and finishers.

questions.stem: A printer finisher keeps jamming when stapling large jobs. What's the most likely fix?
options: Clear the staple jam and check capacity
Replace the network switch the printer uses
questions.explanation: Finishing issues, such as staple jams or hole-punch problems, require clearing the mechanism and staying within capacity limits.

questions.stem: Laser prints show small, random dark spots across pages. What's a likely cause?
options: An incorrect print driver on the PC
A worn pickup roller in the tray
questions.explanation: Speckling often comes from loose toner, a leaking cartridge, or debris on internal components. Cleaning and replacing the cartridge help.

questions.stem: Users can't print to a network printer, but it prints a test page locally. What should be checked?
options: Its network connection and IP address
questions.explanation: If local printing works, the problem is connectivity, such as a changed IP address, network cable, or port settings.

questions.stem: A laser printer makes a grinding noise while feeding paper. What should be checked?
options: The printer's IP address and port
The gears and rollers in the paper path
The toner density setting on the panel
questions.explanation: Grinding noises usually indicate worn gears, damaged rollers, or obstructions in the paper path.
